notes: Prefill tested at S=202751, the longest valid non-aligned logical length; the final position 202751 is exercised through the paged decode path attending the full cache. Together they cover all 202752 positions.
Layer 47 of the checkpoint is the MTP (num_nextn_predict_layers) head; HF's Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM drops it via _keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected, so it is outside the decoder contract.

Decode batch tested up to 32 users (one decode row tile). paged_update_cache is issued in <=16-user groups because its per-core static CBs scale with B*Wt and exceed Blackhole L1 at 32 users x 576 latent width.

fused_decoder.kv_cache_contract: identical to functional_decoder (same paged latent cache ops, dtype, block size, allocation)
fused_decoder.weight_footprint_delta: adds a per-head copy of wq_b for prefill (+7.9 MB bf16 per layer, ~0.36 GiB over 47 layers); wqkv_a replaces wq_a+wkv_a and packed gate_up replaces gate+up at identical byte counts; full-model weights_bf4_experts_bf8_rest_gib_approx 18.5 -> ~18.9, still fits 32 GiB with the bf8 latent cache (5.8 GiB) at batch 1

full_model_projection.fits_32gib_single_chip: yes at batch 1 with bf4 experts and bf8 (or bf16) latent cache
full_model_projection.mha_style_cache_context_ceiling_at_12gib: ~13k tokens - why the latent-cache contract is mandatory

optimized_decoder.kv_cache_contract: identical geometry/ops/indexing to fused_decoder; dtype is now a tested parameter: bfloat16 (comparability arm, same bars as fused) and bfloat8_b (deployment arm; prefill fill tensors typecast to the cache dtype before paged_fill_cache, decode paged_update_cache keeps bf16 inputs; real-weight 202k evidence equal to bf16 within 0.0004 window-agg PCC and equal to the fused real-weight control)

weight_dtype_policy.dense_mlp: bfloat8_b (bf4 measured and rejected: real-weight 202k dense control regression for a ~0.006 ms/tok model-level win)

optimized_decoder.weight_footprint_delta: decode DRAM-sharded copies add ~0.55 GiB over 47 layers at the final dtypes (bf4 attention copies ~9.9 MB + bf4 shared_down ~1.8 MB per moe layer; the dense layer adds its bf8 down copy) on top of the fused stage's wq_b_heads prefill copy; full-model projection at the final policy ~17.5 GiB weights (copies included) + 5.8 GiB bf8 latent cache (or 10.9 GiB bf16) - fits 32 GiB at batch 1 with margin

deployment_arm_real_weights_bf4attn_bf4s.evidence: long_context_{moe,dense}_real_expertbf4_cachebf8.json (+ bit-identical rerun log); every JSON carries an arm provenance block

notes: The optimized decoder is equal-or-better than the fused real-weight control on every 202k window row; sub-0.99 end-window rows at full context are a property of the real checkpoint (present in the fused baseline) and of flip-reconstruction under bf4-expert noise, not an optimization regression.
decode_forward returns the residual width-sharded in L1 (layer-stacking contract); interleaved inputs are resharded automatically.
Synthetic-weight suites run the bf8-attention/bf8-MLP/bf16-cache comparability arm at the 0.995 bar; gaussian weights lose ~2x more than the checkpoint to bf4 block quantization (OPT-012).

current_supported_context_source: full_model stage: whole 47-layer stack + full-context paged latent cache resident on one Blackhole p150-class chip

full_model.measured_allocatable_dram_evidence: 512 MiB DRAM allocations on device 0 until OOM: 31.5 GiB allocated, bank size 4272341376 B x 8 banks (doc/full_model/work_log.md, FM-001)

batch_contract.primary: batch 1 at the full advertised 202752 context (measured, resident)
batch_contract.limit: batch x context is bounded by DRAM: 28764 B/token across 47 layers. Of the 31.5 GiB the allocator hands out (probe/dram_capacity_probe.py), 17.498 GiB is weights + persistent scratch, 0.092 GiB is the sampler's penalty buffers and 0.326 GiB is the reserved trace region, leaving ~13.58 GiB = ~507k total cached tokens. batch 32 x 8192 = 262144 tokens = 7.022 GiB measured resident and fits; batch 32 x 202752 would need 173.8 GiB and is a hard physical limit, not a design choice.

notes: Prefill lengths are bucketed to (128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048) and longer prompts to whole 2048-token chunks plus a bucketed tail; this only pads the physical prefill. The logical prompt length is unrestricted up to 202752 and padded positions are proven not to reach a real one (tests/test_prefill_padding.py: bit-identical logits and generated tokens under two different pad token values, single-chunk and multi-chunk).

Every layer shares one RoPE table set: 47 private copies would add 2.4 GiB of byte-identical data at this context. The decode RoPE index is derived from the current position on device, so there is one position state tensor and an inactive (-1) slot stays pinned at index 0.
